why: issue 2056 (2026-10-25), measured on Nav2's `nav2_velocity_smoother` @jazzy (phase-488 node 2) and over Autoware 0.45.1 (183 files name `std::vector<rclcpp::Parameter>`). OVERRIDDEN, declined -> divergence/adopt-bounded. The recorded reason, "no allocator", is true of a freestanding build and false of the hosted (`NROS_CPP_STD`) build ported code uses. Hosted: `add_on_set_parameters_callback(f)` with `f` over `const std::vector<rclcpp::Parameter>&` returning anything with a `successful` member (upstream's `SetParametersResult`), returning `node_interfaces::OnSetParametersCallbackHandle::SharedPtr` whose destruction unregisters. The proposed write's arrays now cross the FFI (`nros_cpp_param_write_t`'s `*_array` fields), so `as_double_array()` sees the proposed elements. THE BOUND: one write per call, because the store validates writes one at a time, and the `reason` is dropped because the store's hook answers `bool`. The freestanding function-pointer form is unchanged. Previous text: upstream takes a `std::function` over a `std::vector<rclcpp::Parameter>` returning a `SetParametersResult`, and hands back an owning `ParameterCallbackHandle` shared_ptr whose destruction unregisters. With no allocator ours is a plain function pointer plus a `void*` context seeing ONE write at a time as scalars, answering `bool` — upstream's `successful` — and `out_handle` receives a `uint16_t` token because there is nothing to own. The registry is bounded (`nros_params::MAX_ON_SET_CALLBACKS`, 4) and a full one answers `Result::FULL` rather than evicting somebody else's hook. The hook runs AFTER the store's read-only / type / range rules and on every write that reaches the store, local or over `~/set_parameters`, because `apply` is the one seam. RE-VERDICTED phase-417 W4.a. was `gap`, and the capability now SHIPS on `rclcpp::Node`, forwarding to the executor's one `nros_params::ParameterServer` and holding no state of its own. `refuse-loud` rather than `adopt`: the NAME exists, so a ported file reaches it, and the SIGNATURE is what refuses — the compiler names the mismatch at the call site and there is no shape in which this compiles and silently differs.
